newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly by demonstration.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly by demonstration.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was jolted briefly against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday following reports of demonstration in Jakarta, dealers said.
But they said the reaction was shortlived only as it was a peaceful demonstration by supporters of ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri on Tuesday.
Spot rupiah declined to a low of 2,363.50 in the afternoon before it settled at 2,362.40/62.60. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,361.75/62.30 and 2,361.20/61.50, respectively.
Megawati supporters demonstrated in two major cities on Tuesday to demand the right to run in May general elections.

Around 400 members of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) gathered peacefuly at the General Election Institute (LPU) in Jakarta to protest against the body's rejection of Megawati's candidates for the May 29 polls.
In a similar protest in Indonesia's second city of Surabaya, witnesses said more than 2,000 Megawati backers marched peacefully on the East Java office of the election body.
Dealers said this seemed to give some impulse for offshore operators to drive the market but a calm response from local operators appeared to keep the market stable.
They said the focus remained on liquidity which seemed to have eased in the afternoon after turning tight in the morning on the last liquidity reporting day and weekly tax payments.
Overnight money fell to 10.0/11.0 percent from a high of 15.0/15.5 percent. One dealer said expectation for a relaxed condition was reflected in declining tom/next swap rate.
It was last given at 0.5 points. Overnight swap closed at 0.55/0.65 points. One-month swap was at 13.00/14.00, two at 24.75/25.50, three at 37.50/38.50 and six at 77.0/78.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,362/2,554 and the conversion rate at 2,362/2,410 on Tuesday.
